hints.S10_A1: The clue is the list after the dash: WARM BREAD, CINNAMON and BUTTER. Ask: does a BAKERY smell cold, noisy or empty? The blank must describe a smell, so match it to that sugary, comforting scent.
hints.S10_A2: Think how much SALT a dish needs TO IMPROVE ITS FLAVOUR - a bowl, a bucket, a bottle? Ask: how much salt can a CHEF hold between his thumb and one finger? Any more would ruin the whole dish.
hints.S10_A3: AFTER THE BIG MEAL the DISHES are dirty, and they must go back into the CUPBOARD clean. Ask: do 'put off', 'run away' or 'give in' get a single plate clean? A phrasal verb must be learnt as one unit.
hints.S10_A4: The JUDGES gave her FIRST PRIZE, and it was her DREAM COME TRUE. Ask: does the idiom describe someone bursting with joy, or someone ill, in trouble, or confused? An idiom cannot be read word by word.
hints.S10_A5: The clue sits at the end: SMOOTH, with NO MORE LUMPS. Ask: does frying, folding or peeling ever break up lumps? The blank names a quick beating action that smooths a MIXTURE.
hints.S10_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not the COOKING CLASS. Words like nobody and everyone act like ONE person. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain present verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S10_B2: HAS sits right before the blank and needs a partner. Ask: after has, do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? THIS TERM shows it was done recently and still holds now.
hints.S10_B3: The SMOKE ALARM SUDDENLY WENT OFF - it cut across an action already under way. Ask: which form shows an action in progress in the past? FATHER is one person, so the helping verb must be singular.
hints.S10_B4: THAN compares two laksas, and the adjective is short and ends in -y. Ask: does a short adjective take an ending, or 'most' in front? And when a word ends in -y, what must that y turn into first?
hints.S10_B5: The second half explains WHY the noodles TASTED VERY BLAND: NO SEASONING was added at all. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' would give a result, and 'although' would signal a contrast.
hints.S10_B6: A tag mirrors the main verb, and this sentence uses HAS BEEN. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag stay positive or flip to negative? And should it borrow 'did', when the sentence never used that verb at all?
hints.S10_B7: TOO MANY CHILLIES were added BY MISTAKE - it has already happened. Ask: does the verb belong in the past, or is it still going on right now? This verb is regular, so its past is made in the ordinary way.
hints.S10_B8: Two questions settle it: is there one HOT PAN or many, and is it far away or IN MY HANDS? Ask: which pointing word matches a single object right beside the speaker? 'These' and 'those' point at more than one.
hints.S10_C1: TEN O'CLOCK is an exact point on the clock. Ask: which preposition goes before clock times, and which one belongs with parts of the day like 'the morning'? Try each box word aloud before ten o'clock.
hints.S10_C2: MIXED FLOUR ___ BUTTER: two things are being combined into one dough. Ask: which preposition joins the two things you stir together? 'From' shows a source, and 'into' shows a change of form.
hints.S10_C3: The dough CHANGES SHAPE: it begins as a lump and ends as A FLAT SHEET. Ask: which preposition shows a change of form, and which shows only where a thing rests? 'On' and 'in' both show position, not change.
hints.S10_C4: The CIRCLES are taken out of THE SHEET - the sheet is the source they come out of. Ask: which preposition shows where something is taken away? 'In' and 'on' would only show where the circles sit.
hints.S10_C5: A BAKING TRAY is a flat surface, and each TART rests against its top. Ask: which preposition means 'touching the top of a surface', and which means 'inside an enclosed space'? The tarts do not go inside the tray.
hints.S10_C6: An OVEN is an enclosed box with a door, and the TRAY stays within it while it BAKED. Ask: which preposition shows a thing resting inside an enclosed space? The word for a change of form has already been used for the dough.
hints.S10_C7: TWENTY MINUTES tells you how LONG the baking lasted. Ask: which preposition measures a stretch of time, and which one marks an exact point on the clock? 'Until' would need an event after it, not a number.
hints.S10_C8: The waiting stops at the moment THEY TURNED GOLDEN BROWN - an event, not a number of minutes. Ask: which box word means 'up to the point when something happens'? A duration word would need a length of time after it.
hints.S10_D1: Grandma TOOK OUT AN OLD ___ CARD that she had WRITTEN BY HAND years ago, so the blank names something with instructions on it. Ask: which box word names the steps for cooking a dish? An ingredient is a food, not a set of steps.
hints.S10_D2: The clue comes right after: FRESH TURMERIC, WHICH GIVES THE DISH ITS GOLDEN COLOUR. Ask: which box word names ONE food item that goes into a dish? The whole set of instructions is a different word.
hints.S10_D3: The reason is given: SO THAT THERE WOULD BE ENOUGH FOR EVERYONE. Ask: which box word names the amount of food ONE person takes? Leftovers are what remains after a meal, not what you serve at the start.
hints.S10_D4: Notice the verb LOOKED - it describes the CURRY, not the people. Ask: which box word means 'so good-looking that you want to eat it at once'? 'Hungry' would describe MY COUSINS instead.
hints.S10_D5: The reason follows at the end: he had FORGOTTEN TO SPOON ANY CURRY over his RICE. Ask: which box word describes food with almost no flavour? 'Boiling' is about heat, and nobody complained about heat.
hints.S10_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the SIZZLING SOUNDS reaching your ears. Ask: which of the two look-alikes has EAR inside it? They sound the same, so choose by meaning.
hints.S10_E2: Read DECIED letter by letter - two letters have swapped places. Ask: what is the base verb, and what happens when a verb already ends in a silent -e? You add only one letter to it, never two.
hints.S10_E3: CLEANNED has doubled its final consonant. Ask: do we double it in every verb, or only when the word ends in ONE vowel + ONE consonant, like run becoming running? Count the consonants at the end of clean.
hints.S10_E4: EATED forces the regular -ed rule onto an irregular verb. Ask: how would you say it about yesterday? Think of swim becoming swam - the vowel changes, and no ending is added at all.
hints.S10_E5: The NOTEBOOK belongs to the COOKS - more than one person did the cooking. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? When the owners are many, where must the apostrophe go?
hints.S10_F1: The COOKING TEACHER ASKED a yes/no QUESTION and you must now report it. Ask: which small joining word follows asked? Does the reported part keep question order, or normal statement order? And what do 'you' and 'yourself' become?
hints.S10_F2: GRANDMA's action was already under way when the other one broke in. Ask: which sentence is the long background action, and which is the sudden event? WHEN goes in front of the sudden one - and keep the helping verb.
